target_customer: Schools and teachers at first, then companies buying AI personalized workforce training
problem: Learners differ in skill and confidence, and teachers and employers need ways to identify knowledge gaps and personalize learning paths.
business_model: Freemium SaaS: free tier, $9 per month individual plans and schoolwide plans in the K-8 product (2019); later corporate learning subscriptions
product_category: AI personalized learning, education then corporate L&D

founders.name: Maayan Yavne
education: Stanford University (met co-founder as students there in spring 2017)
founders.background_notes: EdSurge (2019-10-30) calls her Israeli and gives an age of 38 at that date; birth year not stated, so age_at_founding is left null.

founders.name: Yael Haramaty
education: Stanford University (met co-founder as students there in spring 2017)
founders.background_notes: YC page names her Yael Cohen Haramaty and describes an EdTech entrepreneur.

technical_complexity.rationale: Adaptive grouping and recommendation of learning resources by proficiency and confidence is standard ML and product work for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Open educational resources and recommendation logic are copyable; no data moat is documented.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Tailor-ED. Later AI features spread across learning platforms per 2025 and 2026 coverage.

market_need_then: EdSurge (2019-10) reports use in over 1,500 schools with 70 paying subscribers, mostly international, showing free usage but weak payment at the time.

identity.logo: A logo file named TE_Logo; design not described.

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand press. The name is confusable with Tailor Brands and a separate New York company called Tailor-Ed, and its education suffix fit the school product less after the corporate pivot.

pivots.from: K-8 math differentiated open educational resources for teachers
pivots.to: AI personalized corporate learning bot integrated with Slack and Teams
pivots.why: Not stated; the YC description (Winter 2019) already pitches corporate learning, while the 2019 EdSurge product was school focused.

outcome_analysis: Tailor-ED raised a $1.6M seed in October 2019 and an extension in September 2021 led by the Israel-Colorado Innovation Fund and Lucas Venture Group, with sources disagreeing on the total from $1.8M to $4.8M. Directories say it ceased operating in November 2024, but no shutdown announcement or cause was found, so the cause is not public.
notes: The GlobeNewswire page returned 403; the 2021 round details come from the search snippet, and its amount is not stated. Total raised conflicts: CB Insights $1.81M, PitchBook $2.56M, StartupNationCentral $4.8M across 3 rounds from 9 investors; a third round may exist and is unrecorded. The shutdown date 2024-11 rests on a single aggregator (Startupim); PitchBook says Out of Business and Dealroom says closed. The company site was reachable but looks stale or spammed (copyright 2023, unrelated gambling links). Founding is May 2018 per Startupim. YC lists the CEO name for Yael as Cohen Haramaty. Competitors left empty because no 2019 dated sources were found.
